entries.notes: Current Three WebGLRenderer checks Object3D.visible before collecting lights. A zero-intensity visible point still influences program key specialization.

entries.name: Markdown Architectural Decision Records (MADR)

entries.name: Technology Radar status model

entries.name: OpenSSF Scorecard
entries.notes: Reuse evaluation dimensions conceptually; do not require the Scorecard CLI for every candidate.

entries.name: Git hooks / core.hooksPath
entries.notes: Already used by this project for local commit-time enforcement.

entries.name: Your Eyes In Space — advertised mit-final tag
entries.license: MIT for mit-final and earlier; current main AGPL-3.0-or-later
entries.notes: Current LICENSE says mit-final and earlier are MIT, but the remote tag is not currently exposed/resolvable. Do not select by tag name; use the separately verified e520568 MIT commit entry.

entries.name: Cosmos browser universe engine
entries.notes: Current MIT main audited locally on 2026-11-22. Strong modular engine: camera-relative coordinates, scale regimes, tile streaming, shaders, tests, thin React canvas. Internal packages compile and Vite bundle runs, but repo-wide typecheck currently fails in SearchPanel on stale ApiEntity fields; full star-tile data also expects a backend manifest. Better subsystem donor than immediate mother product today.

entries.name: Solar Wanderer
entries.notes: Candidate for scale/travel subsystem if a full-solution backbone is not selected.

entries.name: SpaceKit.js
entries.notes: Prefer extracting orbital math/data pieces over adopting its renderer lifecycle wholesale.

entries.name: Galaxy Explorer
entries.notes: Already reused in the current V2 galaxy renderer.

entries.name: Helios procedural star-system generator
entries.notes: Already reused in the current V2 deterministic generator decomposition.

entries.name: ProceduralPlanets
entries.notes: Already integrated; baked mode is the default for scalable ordinary worlds.

entries.name: ProceduralTerrains
entries.notes: Preserved as an optional Hero-surface experiment, not a universal surface requirement.

entries.name: @pmndrs/sky
entries.notes: Potential future WebGPU branch; current main stack is not yet a clean compatibility fit.

entries.name: three-nebula
entries.notes: Candidate effect system; only adopt if the chosen backbone does not already cover these effects.

entries.name: Your Eyes In Space — verified MIT commit e520568
entries.license: MIT source at e520568; bundled HYG-derived stars.bin is CC BY-SA 4.0; NASA assets/data retain their own notices
covers: deterministic procedural star field and systems
entries.notes: Code-level and runtime verified on 2026-11-22: npm ci/build passes; headless browser boots; a minimal public registerExtraSystem patch successfully injected HELION + AURORA-01 and the stock renderer displayed the Hero planet. Main bundle ~2.54 MB; 449 MB dist is dominated by optional lessons/tours (~389 MB) that are not needed for Personal Universe. Additional renderer PoC on 2026-11-22: StarPoints + ProcStarPoints + GalaxyCloud + GalaxySprites + CameraController + Input ran inside the same React Three Fiber 8 / Three 0.185.1 Canvas with logarithmicDepthBuffer; strict TS, Vite build and headless runtime all passed, rendering the 109,401-star catalog without a second canvas.

entries.name: NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP / pscomppars
entries.license: NASA public scientific data / archive terms; attribution retained
entries.notes: Already used by Personal Universe. TAP schema exposes hip_name, hd_name and gaia_dr3_id in pscomppars; 2026-11-22 research found 51/64 nearest snapshot hosts have HIP identifiers and all 51 exactly match the vendored HYG-derived YEIS star binary.

entries.name: React Three Fiber
entries.notes: Current project host. Research PoC proved YEIS renderer classes can attach directly to R3F's existing scene/gl/camera instead of running a second WebGL application.

entries.name: Astro Content Collections / Content Layer
entries.notes: Already available through the installed Astro runtime. Astro 7 provides built-in glob() and file() loaders plus Zod 4 schemas; no new runtime dependency is required for local portfolio content.

entries.name: Keystatic
entries.notes: Good optional authoring UI because it can manage files that Astro Content Collections already consume. Current project does not yet need an embedded editor, so avoid its extra packages/Markdoc/config until authoring friction appears.

entries.name: TinaCMS
entries.notes: Strong visual-editing workflow but existing-site integration adds Tina packages and commonly SSR adapter/island plumbing. Too broad for a static single-owner portfolio content layer at this stage.

entries.name: Decap CMS
entries.notes: Mature Git-based admin UI, but requires an admin surface and backend/auth configuration while still leaving frontend content modeling/placement to the site. Keep as an editor option, not the current foundation.

entries.name: cmdk + Fuse.js navigation/search stack
entries.notes: Candidate supplement only. It would duplicate YEIS astronomical indexes if used as the primary universe navigator.

entries.name: Pagefind
entries.notes: Useful later for article/document search, but not a replacement for YEIS spatial destination search.

entries.name: GitHub Actions PR-diff gate with required status checks
entries.notes: Use the repository-local Node policy engine inside GitHub Actions, but evaluate the PR commit range instead of only a dirty working tree. Pair with a required status check so changing or deleting the workflow cannot silently bypass merge gating.

entries.name: Rendezvous / Highest Random Weight (HRW) hashing
entries.license: Algorithm/reference; RFC text under IETF terms
covers: minimal remapping when destinations are added or removed
entries.notes: Selected as the placement primitive for Personal Signals. Unlike modulo-N, HRW ranks each stable destination identity per content key, so adding/removing a star changes only mappings that genuinely prefer the changed destination.

entries.name: hrw-hash JavaScript package
entries.notes: Very small and dependency-free, but Personal Universe only needs one narrow deterministic score primitive. Prefer the standard HRW algorithm directly to avoid another runtime dependency unless future weighted/ranked APIs justify the package.

entries.name: Jump Consistent Hash
covers: minimal remapping as bucket count changes
entries.notes: Excellent for sequentially numbered buckets, but less appropriate for Personal Universe because star destinations are identity-addressed and can be inserted/removed independently rather than only appended as dense bucket numbers.

entries.name: i18next
entries.notes: Mature generic i18n subsystem. Useful when an application owns its translation resources, but redundant when reusing YEIS data that already ships matching pinned dictionaries and lookup semantics.

entries.name: Browser URLSearchParams + History API
entries.notes: Use for small shareable state that already belongs in the page URL. Prefer this over adding a client router when Personal Universe remains a single Astro page with one existing phase state machine.

entries.name: Three.js BufferGeometry / BufferAttribute capacity management
entries.notes: Three.js documents that rendered buffer attributes cannot be resized in place; when capacity is exceeded, allocate replacement geometry/attributes and dispose superseded GPU resources. Personal Signal overlay uses geometric capacity growth to avoid a fixed ceiling and avoid exact-fit reallocation churn.

entries.name: React Joyride guided-tour product
entries.notes: Mature complete DOM-target onboarding product. Rejected for spatial-universe journeys because its core model targets DOM elements/tooltips and would duplicate Personal Universe destination navigation.

entries.name: XState v5
entries.notes: Strong general orchestration framework. Current guided journey has a deliberately tiny state surface and already shares the destination executor, so adding a second state runtime would be disproportionate.

entries.name: YEIS TourPlayer at verified MIT commit e520568
entries.notes: Reuse only the sequencing semantics needed by Personal Universe. Do not port narration, TTS, timed cues, render overrides, comparison effects, surface pins or simulation-time ownership.

entries.name: React core state/effect hooks
entries.notes: Already present through the project React dependency. Suitable for the small local journey coordinator without introducing a second state framework.

entries.name: Playwright Test
entries.notes: Preferred browser-validation framework for Personal Universe. Reuse Playwright Test for browser lifecycle, assertions, request interception, traces, screenshots and HTML reports instead of maintaining custom CDP/WebSocket smoke tooling.

entries.name: GitHub Pages custom Actions deployment
entries.notes: Preferred no-extra-credential deployment module when repository Pages is enabled for GitHub Actions. Keep deployment independent from PR validation so Pages availability or plan settings do not block CI.

entries.name: Vercel Preview Deployments
entries.notes: Strong per-PR preview product, but requires an external Vercel project/account integration. Keep as a future option if GitHub Pages cannot provide the desired preview ergonomics.

entries.name: Playwright CI sharding across GitHub Actions jobs
entries.notes: Preferred scaling path for the WebGL-heavy suite: keep workers=1 inside each runner, enable fullyParallel for shard balancing, and distribute shards across separate GitHub Actions jobs. This follows Playwright's CI guidance instead of contending multiple SwiftShader browsers on one runner.

entries.name: GitHub Actions matrix strategy
entries.notes: Use matrix jobs to execute Playwright shards on separate hosted runners. This is the CI distribution primitive shown by Playwright's official GitHub Actions sharding example.

entries.name: Three.js Vector3 camera projection
entries.notes: Use the existing Three.js projection primitive to map Personal Signal sky directions to screen coordinates for lightweight hover hit testing. No new runtime dependency.

entries.name: Floating UI virtual elements
entries.notes: Mature DOM floating-position solution and supports cursor/virtual-point anchors. Not selected for Personal Signal hover because WebGL signal hit testing/projection is the hard part and the simple non-interactive label needs only bounded client coordinates.

entries.name: YEIS native body and compact-object travel semantics at verified MIT commit e520568
entries.notes: Reuse the pinned universe/body/camera semantics already hosted inside the R3F canvas. The pinned UI exposes body/system/black-hole travel entry points; Personal Universe should adapt destinations to these primitives rather than inventing a second cross-scale camera path.

entries.name: camera-controls
entries.notes: Mature generic Three.js camera-control library. Not selected for native body travel because it does not own YEIS hierarchical reference frames, native celestial-body identity or system switching; adding it would create a competing camera authority.

entries.name: Astro base path and import.meta.env.BASE_URL
entries.notes: Use Astro's official base configuration and Vite/Astro import.meta.env.BASE_URL for public runtime assets instead of hard-coded root-relative URLs. This preserves root-local development while allowing /personal-universe production hosting.

entries.name: Cloudflare Pages Git integration
entries.notes: Mature root-hosted static deployment fallback. Stronger automatic branch/PR preview ergonomics than GitHub Pages, but requires an external Cloudflare account and GitHub App integration.

entries.name: WebGL context-loss events and WEBGL_lose_context
entries.notes: Use browser-native context-loss events for release failure detection and the standard WEBGL_lose_context extension for deterministic negative-path tests. Drive it through existing Playwright page.evaluate rather than adding a WebGL test framework.

entries.name: Drei useGLTF
entries.notes: Already used by Personal Universe for decorative Three.js assets. Keep asset loading inside the visual branch that actually renders the asset; avoid unconditional preload on software fallback paths that intentionally omit the decoration.
